items.text: Last week one of the demonstrations in France killed two people and hundreds were injured. Last weekend, the grass-roots movement drew the support of 250,000 people across France. The protests are over rising fuel taxes, but the country’s President Emmanuel Macron says that tax rises are needed to reduce the country’s fossil-fuel dependency . Some protesters and many of the anti-government ‘yellow vests’ are also seeking the removal of Emmanuel Macron. The government deployed around 3,000 security personnel in Paris to keep order this weekend. The riot police used tear gas and a water cannon against protesters on the Champs-Elysees after they turned violent. Difficult words: grass-roots movement (a type of bottom-up movement), dependency (the fact of being dependent – needing something too much), seek (try to achieve), removal (removing from office), riot (a violent protest). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Demonstrations started in France last weekend, continued through the week and this weekend. Two people died and hundreds were injured. The protests are over rising taxes on fossil fuels . The French President Emmanuel Macron says that the taxes are needed to reduce the country’s dependency on fossil fuels. Some protesters are also anti-government and they want Macron to step down. Around 3,000 police officers were ready for the protesters in Paris this weekend. The protests turned violent , and police used tear gas and a water cannon against the protesters. Difficult words: fossil fuel (a material like gas, coal and oil which people burn to get or make energy), dependency (being dependent – needing something too much), violent (violent people destroy things and attack other people). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

There are protests in France. People protest high taxes on fossil fuels . Some protesters also want the French president to step down . Two people die in the protests. Hundreds of people are injured. This weekend, there are 3,000 police officers in Paris. They are there because of the protesters. Difficult words: tax (the money which goes to the country when you buy something), fossil fuel (a material like gas, coal and oil which people burn to get energy), step down (stop being something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Someone filmed a massive waterspout in the port of Salerno in south-west Italy, not far from Naples. Nobody was injured as the vortex hit the port, but one Italian news outlet reported that several freight containers were lifted up and thrown around. After hitting land, the waterspout dissolved quickly. Difficult words: waterspout (a rotating column of water – something like a water tornado, but not as strong as a tornado), vortex (a rotating mass of air and water), freight containers (a big box for transporting things on or off of a ship), dissolve (get smaller and smaller until something is gone). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Someone filmed a big waterspout in the port of Salerno in south-west Italy, not far from Naples. Nobody was injured as the vortex hit the port. However, it lifted some freight containers up and threw them around. After hitting land, the waterspout got smaller and smaller and then died off. Difficult words: waterspout (something like a water tornado, but not as strong as a tornado), vortex (a spinning mass of air and water), freight containers (a big box for moving things on or off of a ship). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Salerno is a port in Italy. It is not far from Naples. People film a big waterspout there. No one is injured. However, some containers are thrown around. The waterspout hits the land. It gets smaller and smaller. Then it is gone. Difficult words: port (land close to the water where ships can bring things or pick things up), waterspout (something like a water tornado, but not as strong as a tornado), container (a big box into which you put things to transport on a ship). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A new exhibit showcasing the work of street artist Banksy opened at the MUDEC museum in Milan, Italy. Banksy is known for his anti- capitalism street art, and this is the first time that his work has been publicly displayed. The ‘Flying Copper’, ‘Laugh Now’ and ‘Donut’ are just some of the works in the show named ‘The Art of Banksy. A Visual Protest’ which runs until 14th April 2019. Difficult words: showcase (an exhibit, a display). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A new exhibit called ‘The Art of Banksy. A Visual Protest’ was opened in Milan, Italy. It runs until 14th April 2019. Banksy is known for his anti-capitalism street art, and this is the first time that his work has been publicly displayed . The ‘Flying Copper’, ‘Laugh Now’ and ‘Donut’ are just some of the works on the show. Difficult words: exhibit (an art show), anti-capitalism (against capitalism – a belief that it is good to sell and buy lots of things), publicly (for everybody), display (show to other people). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

There is a new exhibit in Milan, Italy. It is called ‘The Art of Banksy. A Visual Protest’. It runs until 14th April 2019. Banksy is the artist. He is known for his anti-capitalism street art . This is the first time his art is on public display . The ‘Flying Copper’, ‘Laugh Now’ and ‘Donut’ are just some of the works on the show. Difficult words: exhibit (an art show), anti-capitalism street art (art that is against selling and buying lots of things and art that people put out on streets or buildings), public (for everybody), display (a show). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Thousands of migrants recently came together with other migrants on the 2,500-kilometre trip north to the US border from the south of Mexico. Many are running away from poverty , gang violence, and political instability in their countries. In Mexico, hundreds of migrants got on a cage truck headed northbound. Cage trucks normally transport animals, but now they also transport people who want to go to the US. One father, Miguel, is travelling with his pregnant wife, Marjorie, and their baby son from Honduras to ‘look for a better future’ because Honduras ‘will always be the same’. In Honduras, they work just to have something to eat and that is only sometimes, adds his wife. Another migrant, Maria Isabel Reyes, said that she was happy that they were making their trip north even if the journey was slow. Difficult words: poverty (when you are poor and it is hard to get out of the situation of being poor), political instability (when the government in a country keeps changing or its leaders cannot run the country well). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

At the southern border of Mexico, thousands of migrants came together on the 2,500-kilometre trip north to the US border. Many are running away from poverty , gang violence, and political instability in their countries. Hundreds of migrants are riding on a cage truck going north. Cage trucks normally move animals, but now they also move people. One father is travelling with his pregnant wife and their baby son from Honduras to try to get a better future because Honduras is not going to get better. Another migrant was happy to head north even if the journey was slow. Difficult words: border (the line between countries), poverty (when you cannot get out of the situation of being poor), political instability (when the government in a country has a lot of problems). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In southern Mexico, thousands of migrants come together. Their countries have problems. They want to go the USA. They are going on a 2,500-kilometre trip. They are going north to the US border . Hundreds of migrants ride on a cage truck . Cage trucks are normally for animals. Now they are also for people. One family is from Honduras. The father goes with his pregnant wife. They also have a baby son. They want to have better lives. They say that Honduras is not going to get better. Difficult words: migrant (a person who travels from one country to another to live there), border (the line between countries), cage truck (a very big truck that has a lot of cages and space for animals). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In south-east London last June, 40-year-old Aaron Ali hit two pensioners with his $12,000 mobility scooter while they waited for a bus. Courts convicted Ali of two counts of Actual Bodily Harm , and he went to jail for two years. Difficult words: pensioner (a person who receives a pension after he or she reaches an old enough age to stop working – a pension money from the government), mobility scooter (an electronic scooter for people who have trouble with walking or cannot walk), convict (find that you committed a crime), count (a crime that you commit), Actual Bodily Harm (a term in the UK for when you hurt someone and intend to do it). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In London, a 40-year-old man hit two older women with his mobility scooter while they were waiting for a bus. Courts convicted the man of Actual Bodily Harm and he went to jail for two years. Difficult words: mobility scooter (an electronic scooter or wheelchair), convict (find that you are guilty of a crime), Actual Bodily Harm (a UK word for when you hurt someone and plan to do it). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In London, two older women are waiting for a bus. A man comes up in his mobility scooter . He hits them and hurts them. People find that he is guilty of Actual Bodily Harm . The man goes to jail for two years. Difficult words: mobility scooter (an electronic scooter or wheelchair), Actual Bodily Harm (a UK word for when you hurt someone and you want to do it). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Parts of North-eastern America are experiencing the first snowfall of the season which has caused travel disruptions and closed schools. Some areas have had up to six inches (15 centimetres) of snow fall last week. On the other hand, at least one of the American residents enjoyed the snow – panda BeiBei at the Smithsonian Zoo in Washington. Someone filmed her playing in the snow. The snow, sleet and rain come as California continues to deal with deadly wildfires. Difficult words: disruption (something which disrupts something – makes problems), resident (a person/animal that resides/lives somewhere), sleet (rain with ice/snow). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Parts of North-eastern America are experiencing the first snowfall of the season. The snow, sleet and rain caused travel disruptions and closed schools. In some areas, up to six inches (15 centimetres) of snow fell last week. On the other hand, at least one of the American residents enjoyed the snow. It was panda BeiBei at the Smithsonian Zoo in Washington. Someone filmed her playing in the snow. The winter weather comes as California continues to deal with deadly wildfires. Difficult words: sleet (rain with ice/snow), disruption (something which disrupts something – makes problems), resident (a person/animal that resides/lives somewhere). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Winter arrives in parts of the USA. Up to six inches (15 centimetres) of snow fall in North-eastern America. This causes problems with traffic. Some schools close. However, not everybody sees the weather as a problem. Panda BeiBei likes the snow. She lives at the Smithsonian Zoo in Washington. She plays in the snow. In the north-east, it is winter. In California, however, people are still fighting wildfires . The situation is not good there. Difficult words: arrive (come), cause (make), wildfire (a large fire which burns forests and houses). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Police stopped a man in Arkansas for a traffic violation last Sunday; Arkansas is a state in the American South. Moments after stopping, the man opened fire on the police officer who started shooting back at him. The video filmed from the police car also shows an SUV approaching and stopping at the scene, but then backing up quickly as if to have nothing to do with the shooting. After about a minute of shooting, the man got back in his car and drove away. Luckily, no one was seriously hurt in the incident, and police arrested the driver later that day. Difficult words: traffic violation (an offence – doing something illegal on the road), open fire (start shooting), SUV (a sport utility vehicle – a bigger four-wheel drive car), approach (come). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Arkansas is a state in the American South, and the police stopped a man there for a traffic violation last Sunday. Moments after stopping, he opened fire on the police officer. The officer started firing back at him. A camera in the police car filmed the incident. The video also shows another car approach and stop at the scene . Then, it quickly backs up to get away from the danger. After about a minute of shooting, the man got back in his car and drove away. Luckily, no one was seriously hurt in the incident. Police arrested the driver later that day. Difficult words: traffic violation (an offence – doing something illegal on the road), approach (come), scene (the place where something happens). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Arkansas is a state in the American South. Police stop a car there. The car stops. The driver starts to shoot at the policeman. The policeman shoots back. A camera in the police car films the incident . The shooting goes on for about a minute. Then the man gets back in his car. He drives away. Later police arrest him. Difficult words: incident (a very good or bad event), arrest (take to a police station). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The Sri Lankan president dissolved the country’s parliament and ousted the prime minister in favour of his preferred candidate. The president also called for fresh elections on 5th January to try and secure backing for his new PM. Politicians and civilians gathered in Colombo, the country’s capital, last Sunday evening for a candlelit vigil to protest the president’s decision. The mayor of Colombo said that it was pretty evident that people who never come to protest decided to mark their presence simply because they feel that democracy has been taken away from their country. Difficult words: dissolve (close, end), oust (remove from a position), fresh (new), backing (support), gather (come together in large numbers), vigil (a calm, peaceful demonstration). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The Sri Lankan president dissolved the country’s parliament and removed the prime minister from office. He made someone that he likes the prime minster instead. Politicians and civilians came together in Colombo, the country’s capital, last Sunday for a candlelit vigil . They protested the president’s actions, and the mayor of Colombo spoke to the media. She said that people feel that the president took democracy away from their country. Due to this, people who normally do not protest came to the vigil. Difficult words: dissolve (close, end), civilian (a person who is not in the military or politics), vigil (a calm, peaceful demonstration). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

This news is about Sri Lankan politics. The Sri Lankan president removes the prime minister. He dissolves the parliament, too. He makes somebody that he likes a new prime minister. People do not like this. They feel that this is not democratic . They organise a vigil . They come together with candles. Even people, who normally do not protest, go to the vigil. Difficult words: remove (put away), dissolve (remove, close, end), democratic (when the people of a country decide its leaders or laws), vigil (a calm, peaceful demonstration). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Stan Lee, an American comic book writer, editor, and publisher, active from the 1940s to the 2010s, has passed away at the age of 95. He was Marvel Comics’ primary creative leader for two decades, and he led a small division of a publishing house to a multimedia corporation that dominates the comics industry. In collaboration with other writers and artists, he co-created many popular characters, including superheroes like Spider-Man, the X-Men, Iron Man, Thor, the Hulk, the Fantastic Four, Black Panther, Daredevil, Doctor Strange, and Ant-Man. Difficult words: pass away (die), division (a part of an organisation/company), publishing house (a company which publishes books or comic books), in collaboration (working together). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Stan Lee was an American comic book writer, editor, and publisher that was active from the 1940s to a 2010s. He has passed away at the age of 95. He co-created very popular characters , especially superheroes like Spider-Man, the X-Men, Iron Man, Thor, the Hulk, the Fantastic Four, Black Panther, Daredevil, Doctor Strange, and Ant-Man. Difficult words: pass away (die), co-create (create/make together with other people), character (a person in a book or a film). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

This news is about Stan Lee. He is an American comic book writer. His career starts in the 1940s. It ends in the 2010s. This year, he dies. He is 95. Many people know his characters from films and comic books. He co-creates them with other writers. They are superheroes like Spider-Man, the X-Men, Iron Man, Thor, the Hulk, the Fantastic Four, Black Panther, Daredevil, Doctor Strange and Ant-Man. Difficult words: character (a person in a book or a film), co-create (create/make together with other people). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Australia, an 18-person team of medical professionals successfully separated 15-month-old conjoined twins from Bhutan after 6 hours of surgery. The girls, named Nima and Dawa, were joined at the lower chest, pelvis , and shared their liver. Doctors had not been sure if the girls shared a bowel and once they started the procedure, they had to reconstruct the twins’ abdomens . Now the babies are recovering at the Royal Children’s Hospital in Melbourne. Difficult words: conjoined (joined together), pelvis (the bones between the middle of the body and the legs that hold up the body), bowel (the canal below the stomach), abdomen (the middle of the body). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Fifteen-month old conjoined twins from Bhutan came to hospital in Australia for a special surgery. The girls were joined at the lower chest , the lower body, and shared an organ. Doctors were not sure if the girls shared other organs too. Once the doctors started the surgery, they had to rebuild their abdomens . The team of 18 medical professionals successfully separated them after 6 hours. The babies are now getting better in the hospital. Difficult words: conjoined twins (when two siblings are born at the same time and share a part of their bodies with one another), chest (the part between the neck and stomach), separate (turn into two parts), abdomen (the middle of your body). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Conjoined twin girls are born in Bhutan. They share parts of their bodies with one another. It can be hard to survive if you are a conjoined twin. Now they are 15 months old. Their mother takes them to Australia to get surgery. The surgery can separate them. Eighteen doctors and professionals help the girls. They take 6 hours to do the surgery. The girls have only one abdomen . The doctors must make each baby a new abdomen. The surgery goes well. The girls are getting better. Difficult words: conjoined twins (when two brothers or sisters are born at the same time and they share parts of their bodies together), survive (live through a difficult time), separate (turn into two normal babies), abdomen (the middle of your body – where food goes after you eat it). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In California, wildfires are raging again and strong winds and dry forests mean that the flames spread over 177 kilometres and destroy thousands of buildings. Around 250,000 people have been forced to flee and at least nine people died – five of them found dead in burned-out vehicles after attempting to flee. Hollywood stars are included in those who have lost their homes due to the blazes and the city of Malibu has been entirely evacuated. A town called Paradise of 30,000 residents has been completely destroyed. Difficult words: rage (continue to exist with great force), flee (get away, run away), attempt (try), due to (because of), blaze (a very large fire), resident (a person who resides – lives somewhere). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

There are wildfires in California again because the forests are dry and the winds are strong. They spread fires quickly, and over 177 kilometres of land burns. Thousands of buildings burn down and one town called Paradise is completely destroyed. Around 30,000 people lived there. Around 250,000 people have to flee . Nine or more people die – five of them are found dead in their burned-out cars. In Malibu, the homes of Hollywood stars burn down, too. Everybody from Malibu is evacuated. Difficult words: spread (grow), flee (get away, run away). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

There are wildfires in California again. The forests are dry. The winds are strong. Fires spread fast because of this. Over 177 kilometres of land burns. Thousands of buildings burn down. One town of 30,000 people is completely destroyed. Around 250,000 people flee . Nine people die. Five of them die in their cars. Difficult words: wildfire (a large dangerous fire which burns forests and buildings), spread (grow), flee (get away, run away). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

David Schwimmer, the actor from the TV show ‘Friends’, went on Twitter to clear his name when a security camera caught his lookalike stealing beer. People from all over the world noticed the uncanny resemblance . Schwimmer added that the doppelgänger could not be him because he was in New York when the other man was in Blackpool, England. He wished the police good luck in finding the thief. Difficult words: uncanny (unusual), resemblance (looking like something else), doppelgänger (a German word for a person that looks just like you). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A thief who looks incredibly like David Schwimmer (an actor from the TV show ‘Friends’) was filmed on camera. The video of the man stealing beer got on the Internet and people soon noticed. In fact, they did not know whether it was or was not the star, so Schwimmer posted on Twitter that he was innocent – the crime took place in England while he was in New York. He wished the police good luck in catching the beer thief. Difficult words: incredibly (very), innocent (not guilty of a crime – not in trouble). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In England, a man steals beer. A security camera films him. People see the video. They put it online. They say that this man looks like David Schwimmer. Schwimmer is a TV actor. He is famous for his role in ‘Friends’. He goes on Twitter. He wants to clear his name. He says that it is not him stealing the beer. He says that he is in New York when this man is in England. He wishes the police good luck in finding the thief . Difficult words: lookalike (someone who looks like you), clear one’s name (say that you did not commit a crime), thief (a person who steals – takes something from a shop without paying for it). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Barcelona, Spain, a ferry sparked a fire when it crashed into a crane. The ferry operator blamed “strongly adverse weather conditions” for the crash. Four hundred and fourteen people were on board the ferry; fortunately, none were hurt. Difficult words: spark (start), blame (say that something is its fault), adverse (very bad). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In Barcelona Spain, a ferry started a fire after it crashed into a crane . The ferry operator said that “strongly adverse weather conditions” made it difficult to control the boat. Four hundred and fourteen people were on the ferry. Luckily, none of them were hurt. Difficult words: ferry (a boat that moves people or things), crane (a big and tall structure for moving heavy things), adverse (very bad). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A ferry is in a harbour in Barcelona, Spain. It crashes into a crane . This starts a fire. The ferry driver says that the weather is bad. This is why the ferry crashes. Four hundred and fourteen people are on the ferry. No one is hurt. Difficult words: ferry (a boat that moves people or things), harbour (a place by the sea where people or things come on ships), crane (a big and tall structure for moving heavy things). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In the north east of Italy, severe storms, wind, and rain damaged the area and killed at least 14 people. Many of them died in car accidents or after debris or falling trees hit them. The storms filled up dams, knocked down trees, flooded homes, and caused mudslides that blocked roads or made buildings fall down hills. Italy’s fire and rescue service released drone videos so that people could know of the impact . Difficult words: severe (extreme), debris (pieces of broken things), impact (the full consequence/effect of something). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In Italy, extreme storms, wind, and rain caused damage and killed at least 14 people. Many of them died from debris or falling trees. The storms filled up dams , knocked down trees, flooded homes, and created mudslides that blocked roads and made buildings fall down hills. Italy’s fire and rescue service showed videos so that people could know what happened. Difficult words: debris (pieces of broken things), dam (a lake which holds water because people built a wall), mudslide (when water causes the land to move like water). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

There are terrible storms in Italy. There is a lot of wind and rain. All of this kills at least 14 people. The people die in car accidents. Pieces of things hit them. Trees fall on them. The storms fill up dams . Trees fall down. Houses go under water. Mudslides fall on roads. Mudslides make buildings fall down hills. Difficult words: terrible (very bad), dam (a lake which holds water because people built a wall), mudslide (when water makes the land move like water). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Jakarta, Indonesia, a passenger plane crashed in the sea, killing all 189 people on board. Plane’s pilot had asked for permission from the airport to turn back, but 13 minutes later, the airport lost contact. People are searching for survivors, but they have found human remains and personal belongings. Hundreds of divers are searching along the seabed , and specialised ships equipped with sonar are also searching the wreckage . The cause of the crash is still unclear. Difficult words: remains (small pieces of a body), seabed (the ocean floor), sonar (a system that uses sound for measuring things under the water), wreckage (what is left of a vehicle or a building after a disaster). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In Jakarta, Indonesia, a pilot was flying a plane. He asked to return to the airport, but 13 minutes later, the airport lost contact with the plane. People discovered that the plane had crashed in the sea, and all 189 people on board died. People are looking for survivors, but they have found only human remains and personal items . Divers are looking along the seabed , and ships are using sonar to search the crash. The cause of the crash is still unknown. Difficult words: remains (small parts of a body), item (a thing), seabed (the ground of the ocean), sonar (using sound to measure things under the water). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A pilot is flying a plane in Jakarta, Indonesia. The pilot asks the airport to return the plane to the ground. Then the airport loses contact with the plane. The plane crashes in the sea. All 189 people on the plane die. People are looking for survivors . There are divers and boats with sonar . They only find dead people and their things. People still do not know why the plane crashed . Difficult words: survivor (someone who lives through a difficult situation), diver (a person who dives – swims deep under the water), sonar (a special piece of technology which uses sound so people can see under the water), crashed (past of ‘crash’ – fall down or into something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Twenty-two-year-old Kierah Lagrave was slapped on her behind by her friend at a New York nightclub. She did not know that this was her girlfriend, and she thought that it was the club’s bouncer instead. The 155-centimetre girl was not having any of that and she went for the bouncer. She grabbed him from behind and choked him until he was unconscious . Police charged her with strangling but later released her. Police said that the bouncer did not resist because he thought it was a friend playing a joke. Difficult words: bouncer (a nightclub security guard), not have any of that (dislike something a lot), go for (do something or attack someone suddenly), grab (take and hold), choke (press on the neck), unconscious (so that the person collapses, ‘falls asleep’), charge (officially say that somebody did something illegal), strangling (squeezing the neck). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

At a New York nightclub a 22-year-old woman’s friends lapped her on her behind. She did not know that her girlfriend slapped her – she thought that it was the bouncer . The 155-centimetre girl was not having any of that and she went for the bouncer. She started choking him until he fell to the ground. Police arrested the woman, but she was free to go. Police said that the bouncer did not do anything because he thought that it was a friend playing a joke. Difficult words: bouncer (a nightclub security guard), not have any of that (dislike something), go for (do something or attack suddenly), choke (press on the neck). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Two women are at a bar in New York. They are friends. One slaps the other on her behind. The other woman does not know this. She does not know that her friend slaps her. She does not see it. She thinks it is the bouncer . She gets angry. She goes up to him. She starts to choke him from behind. The bouncer falls to the ground. Police arrest the woman, but later they let her go. Difficult words: slap (hit with the hand), bouncer (a nightclub security guard), choke (press on the neck). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Police arrested Asia Bibi in 2009 in Pakistan after people accused her of blasphemy following a quarrel with two fellow female farm workers who refused to drink from a water container used by a Christian. A few days later, a mob accused her of insulting Islam’s Prophet which led to her conviction in 2010. The court charged her with blasphemy and sentenced to death. After spending eight years on death row, the court acquitted her. The court’s decision sparked a protest – hundreds of people marched in the streets. One of the protesters, the president of Jamaat-e-Islami (a socially conservative Islamist political party) said that there was pressure from Britain, America and the Pakistani government, but this was the matter of the honour of their beloved Prophet. On the other hand, Tahira Abdullah, a human rights activist, said that the Supreme Court of Pakistan rendered an excellent judgement which will set precedent for decades or even centuries to come in the judicial history of Pakistan. Mrs Bibi now plans to leave the country. Difficult words: blasphemy (speaking badly about God), quarrel (an angry argument), mob (a group of ordinary and angry people), acquit (free), spark (start), render (deliver, give), precedent (a court’s decision which is usually followed in similar cases). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Asia Bibi is a Christian woman from Pakistan. In 2009, she got into an argument with farm workers. As they did not want to drink from a container that she drank from because she is Christian. A few days later, people said that she insulted Islam’s Prophet. Blasphemy is punished by death in Pakistan and the court sentenced her in 2010. She spent eight years waiting to be killed, but the court freed her instead. This made some people angry and hundreds of them protested in the streets of Karachi. Mrs Bibi’s plans now are to leave the country. Difficult words: container (a thing which can hold water), insult (say something bad somebody/something), blasphemy (speaking badly about God). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Asia Bibi is from Pakistan. She is Christian. In 2009, she gets in trouble. People say that she says bad things about Islam’s Prophet. This is a very serious crime in Pakistan. The court sentences her to death. This happens in 2010. In 2018, she is not killed. The court sets her free. This makes some people angry. Hundreds of people protest. Mrs Bibi’s plans now are to leave the country. Difficult words: court (people who tell you if you are a criminal or not), sentence (say what a criminal must do). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Spanish artist Enrique Tenreiro defaced Franco’s tombstone with a red dove and the slogan ‘For Freedom’ last Wednesday. The incident took place at Franco’s final resting place, the Valley of the Fallen, which is a vast monument dedicated to the 30,000 people who died during the Spanish Civil War. After the war, Francisco Franco went to rule Spain with an iron fist until his death in 1975. People know the sculptor and video artist for provocative acts – once he rode in a glass elevator while sitting on a bidet. As guards led him away from the scene, people could hear him shouting, ‘For freedom and the reconciliation of all Spaniards’. Francisco Franco ruled Spain as a dictator from 1939 to 1975. He came to power after he won the Spanish Civil War, and people buried him at a monument dedicated to 30,000 people who died during this war. Spanish artist Enrique Tenreiro drew a red dove and the slogan ‘For Freedom’ on Franco’s tombstone last Wednesday. Tenreiro is a sculptor and video artist known for provocative acts – once he rode in a glass elevator sitting on a bidet. As guards led him away from the tomb, he shouted, ‘For freedom and the reconciliation of all Spaniards’. Difficult words: dedicated (it is for them, to show respect), tombstone (a large flat stone laid over a grave), reconciliation (coming together, becoming ‘friends’ again). This news is about Spain. From 1936 to 1939, there is a war. It is the Spanish Civil War . Around 30,000 people die. The side with Francisco Franco wins the war. Franco becomes a dictator. He is a dictator in Spain until he dies in 1975. There is a big monument in Spain. It shows respect to the 30,000 dead people. Franco is buried there, too. He has a tombstone there. An artist comes to this tombstone. He draws a red dove and writes ‘For Freedom’ on the tombstone. Difficult words: civil war (a war between the people of one country), tombstone (a large flat stone laid over a grave), dove (a bird which is a symbol of peace – no war or fighting). At a safari park in Crimea, three adorable white tigers were recently born. They are now one week old. They are beginning to open their eyes. In 2009, the park’s first white tigers arrived, and now it is home to 12, including the little, extremely cute, furry siblings. There are only 200 white tigers surviving in the wild, so the new arrivals are extremely welcome. Difficult words: adorable (cute, sweet), furry (hairy). Six hundred years ago, Spain’s monarchy first allowed shepherds to move their livestock based on the seasons. On Sunday of this year, there was a rural feel in Madrid, Spain, as shepherds herded over 2,000 sheep for the Fiesta de la Trashumancia. In 1993, people resurrected this festival to celebrate shepherds moving their flocks for the winter. Madrid’s mayor welcomes the sheep, and people pay him to let them through. Difficult words: monarchy (the king or queen and other rulers of a country), rural feel (when a place feels traditional and closer to nature, like a small town or a farm), resurrect (resume, start something again). You can watch the video news lower on this page.
